text:
mara: quick question — for the collector redesign, are we leaning toward per-signal pipelines on the agent, or pushing signal sharding to gateway?
jonas: leaning gateway for now. reasons: single place for exporter fanout + easier quota enforcement (per-customer).
wei: gateway has ops complexity though. more network hops and potential for backpressure spikes. agent-local pipelines give better tail latency.
sam: can we do hybrid? keep traces local (to preserve KV cache locality) and route metrics/logs to gateway for aggregation?
mara: hybrid sounds plausible. main tradeoff i care about is cache hit rate for span KV vs duplication costs when we fanout at gateway.
jonas: agreed. also retention policy differences — if gateway handles retention windows we can offload storage tier decisions there. agents shouldn't know retention tiers.
wei: but retention tags need to travel with the span. that means adding routing metadata at agent or a tiny compute stage at gateway to map tenant->retention. overhead? small but measurable.
sam: what about throttles and quotas? We prefer enforce-as-close-to-source as possible, else contention at gateway. But agent enforcement can be bypassed if someone spoofs requests.
mara: let's enumerate scenarios: (1) agent enforces per-route quotas but gateway double-checks global quotas; (2) gateway enforces only. Which is simpler to roll out?
jonas: (1) is gradual rollout friendly. agents can start applying soft quotas, gateway will be authoritative. console UX for rollouts: show both agent and gateway enforcement points.
wei: implementation sketch for agent pipeline config:
```yaml
pipelines:
  traces:
    processors: [batch, kvcache]
    exporters: [local-buffer, gateway]
  metrics:
    processors: [metric-agg]
    exporters: [gateway]
```
jonas: gateway routing policy POC idea: route by tenant hash % N_shards, then within shard decide exporter set (cold vs hot storage). keeps fanout bounded.
sam: important: when gateway fans out to multiple exporters for the same trace, we must preserve ordering for spans within a trace to avoid downstream confusion. that implies per-trace sequencing tokens or using buffered connections.
mara: ops question: how do we surface this in Console? I want a single-pane view that highlights which pipelines are agent-only, hybrid, or gateway-only, plus per-tenant cost estimate.
jonas: we can add a topology tab under Telemetry -> Collector with a per-route map. Also link to rollouts so SEs can stage config changes (canary to 5% agents then 50%).
wei: backpressure model: if gateway is overloaded we should signal agents to shed non-critical signals (metrics) but keep traces. need a light control channel (gRPC control stream).
infra-bot: deploy status: canary agents updated in us-west-2 on 2025-11-03 14:02 UTC.
sam: last nit: exporter credentials. If agents can talk directly to cloud exporters, we need short-lived creds or proxy through gateway. prefer gateway-proxy for enterprise/private deployments.
mara: summary: propose hybrid default — traces local-first with gateway overflow/fanout, metrics/logs gateway-first. agent soft-quotas + gateway authoritative. add Console topology + rollout UX. any objections?
jonas: none from me, will draft design doc.
wei: +1, i'll prototype control stream behavior.
sam: +1, will check enterprise credential flow.
mara: thanks all, i'll open the RFC and link to this thread.
